newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil tumbles with futures, slow demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil tumbles with futures, slow demand.

text.p: NWE fuel oil lost ground sharply on Thursday amid slow demand and weaker crude.
"No one can say anything about fuel that would counteract crude's weakness," said one trader.

High sulphur cracked barges traded at $117, $116 and $115 fob ARA, failing to get any support from reasonable bunker demand. Pressure to sell product before the end of the month, good stocks of Russian material and a motive to push the market lower in anticipation of pricing a large cargo were all bearish factors.
High sulphur cracked cargoes were also lower, trading down to $114 fob NWE because of sparse buying interest from end-users.
With several important utility buyers having the capacity to take straight run with moderate water content the cracked market is being dominated by good supplies of Russian material.

Low sulphur was a touch softer but marginally firmer than swaps of $122-123 for November. Dealers said a possible arbitrage to the U.S could give support although no trades have been seen yet. A large low sulphur cargo was believed sold yesterday despite some talk that it had been withdrawn. Low sulhur straight run was easier in line with crude.
